analysis.title: High CPI but probably not in itself enough to tip the scales for October
key_insights: September core CPI rose 0.33% m/m (2.6% y/y), above consensus of 0.2% m/m and 2.5% y/y. It is the second consecutive upside surprise.

The upside surprise was broadly based. Core goods (0.25%, 0.18% ex used cars and trucks) and rents (0.33%) were each 0.1-0.15 percentage points above SEB's forecast, and services ex-rents were also higher than expected.
Air tickets (1.2%) and hotels (2.0%) contributed to faster price increases but both slowed from the previous month.
The 3-month annualized core CPI change is back above 3%, at the high end of the recent range. SEB says this may concern Fed members who focus on that measure.
Headline CPI rose 0.6% m/m and 3.7% y/y, in line with consensus on the monthly figure. Energy rose about 5% m/m, slightly less than SEB forecast, and food was unchanged.
SEB's preliminary estimate for September core PCE is 0.31% m/m. The September PPI due the next day will add input.
Several Fed members want to assess the effects of the September rate hike before tightening again, most likely at the December meeting. This raises the bar for a hike at the 28 October meeting.
Market pricing for an October hike moved from about 20% before the CPI to almost 50% after it.
SEB keeps its call for an unchanged rate in October. It says the totality of data this week (PPI, retail sales, industrial production, Beige Book), Middle East events and energy prices will decide.
August retail sales surprised strongly to the upside. A strong September report could signal more scope for companies to pass costs on to customers.

Fed Chair Warsh has been hawkish at Jackson Hole and after the September meeting, and his comments have tended to raise rate-hike expectations. He and IMF head Georgieva have a fireside chat early Friday.

SEB sees short-term upside inflation risks from renewed energy price increases (indirect effects such as transportation costs), emerging goods price increases and possible re-acceleration in market-based Zillow rents.
Wage inflation continues to slow. SEB expects underlying inflation to improve as tariff, energy and AI build-out impulses fade, with core CPI and core PCE back at target by the end of 2028.

risk_factors: Renewed energy price increases could delay the headline inflation slowdown and cause indirect effects through transportation costs.
Goods prices are showing signs of increasing.
Rents may re-accelerate, judging by market-based Zillow rents, driven by worsening home purchase affordability from higher mortgage rates.
A strong September retail sales report could signal more pricing power for companies.
A hawkish Warsh could raise rate-hike expectations further.
The inflation outlook is significantly more uncertain than normal.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case for a hike: core CPI surprised up two months running, the 3-month annualized rate is above 3%, goods and rents are firming, and Warsh has said the CPI slowdown did not meaningfully improve the trend. Markets price almost 50%.
tension_points.bear_case: Several Fed members want to evaluate the September hike before tightening again, most likely in December. Wage inflation continues to slow, which implies any inflation upturn will be temporary.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hawkish call would be strengthened by strong PPI, retail sales and industrial production later this week, or higher energy prices. SEB says the totality of the week's data will decide.
